title: Enterprise pitch kit and competitive heatmap - 2026
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
Redwood Inference helps engineering-led enterprise teams deliver consistent, cost-predictable LLM features across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This kit is a single-page resource for AE/SE teams to: 1) position Redwood vs cloud and endpoint competitors, 2) present a concise enterprise pitch deck (8 slides), 3) surface pricing guidance and a simple TCO model, 4) answer top security/ops questions, and 5) share a short customer case vignette with quantified benefits.

Why this matters (one-liner):
Deliver production-grade inference with predictable latency, lower per-token cost, and unified tooling across environments—without building and operating a bespoke serving stack.

Primary audience:
- Technical buyers: ML Platform, ML Engineering, Infrastructure
- Economic buyers: Head of Engineering, CTO, CFO
- Champions: Product/Eng managers building LLM features

Positioning pillars (3):
- Production-first economics: measurable per-token cost reductions with caching, batching, and quantization recommendations tied to actual traffic patterns.
- Unified runtime across deployment modes: same API, same rollout and observability for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Reliability and graceful degradation: automated model fallbacks, regional routing, and fast canary rollouts to reduce customer outages.

Key messages by persona:
- ML Platform/Eng: "Use a runtime designed for inference—KV cache, continuous batching, and kernel selection save ops time and improve throughput. We integrate with your CI and infra standards."
- Product/PM: "Ship consistent UX: streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs with low tail latency."
- Finance/CIO: "Lower unit costs and predictable reserved capacity options; flexible private deployments for regulated data."

Competitive heatmap (summary view):
Legend: ✓ = strong, ~ = mixed, ✗ = weak
| Capability                          | Redwood Inference | Large cloud AI providers | Self-hosted open runtimes | LLM API-only providers |
|------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------|---------------------------|------------------------|
| Predictable reserved capacity      | ✓                 | ~                        | ✗                         | ✗                      |
| Unified API across environments    | ✓                 | ~                        | ✗                         | ✓                      |
| Cost optimization tooling          | ✓                 | ~                        | ✗                         | ✗                      |
| Enterprise private deployments     | ✓                 | ~                        | ~                         | ✗                      |
| Production observability / SLOs    | ✓                 | ~                        | ✗                         | ✗                      |
| Fast model onboarding & evals      | ✓                 | ~                        | ✓                         | ✗                      |
| SLA-backed latency & uptime        | ✓                 | ✓                        | ✗                         | ✗                      |

Notes on competitors: 
- Large cloud AI providers (major hyperscalers) offer integrated infra and enterprise contracts; they are strong on scale and account management but often lag on inference-specific cost controls and inference-optimized runtimes.
- Open self-hosted runtimes provide control but require significant engineering investment (serving, autoscaling, SRE).
- API-first LLM vendors are easiest to adopt but lack private deployment options and enterprise reserved capacity.

Suggested objection handling (short):
- "We can build this ourselves": Point to measured dev+ops cost to reach parity (months of engineering, ongoing SRE). Offer an architecture workshop and a 30-day pilot with baseline benchmarks.
- "Hyperscaler gives us scale": Acknowledge scale advantage; emphasize cost-per-token and dedicated GPU throughput optimizations plus multi-region fallback and private deployment parity.
- "Security / compliance concerns": Provide reference architecture, SOC2 evidence, and KMS/HSM integrations in the appendix. Offer a joint security review during the pilot.

8-slide pitch deck (one-liner per slide):
1. Cover: value proposition + customer logo(s) (if permitted).
2. Problem: the operational burden of running LLM inference at scale (latency, cost, regression risk).
3. Redwood solution: unified runtime + routing + observability across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
4. How it works at a glance: serving runtime, cache/batching, compilation/kernel selection, routing policies.
5. ROI example: customer case (see below) with measured latency and cost improvements.
6. Security & compliance: private deployments, KMS, audit logging, SOC2 evidence.
7. Partnership model & pricing summary (high-level tiers).
8. Next steps & pilot proposal: 30-day pilot, success criteria, owners.

Pricing guidance (high-level):
- Hosted (self-serve): pay-as-you-go per-token pricing; entry tier for dev/proof-of-concept with free credits.
- Dedicated (reserved): monthly committed GPU pools with discounted per-token tiers and burst capacity; typical enterprise contract: 12–36 months with committed throughput and optional managed upgrades.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform license + optional managed services; pricing includes base seat/cluster fee + support tier.

Anchor rates (example for sales conversations, adjust with deal team):
- Hosted gen: $0.0008–$0.002 per token depending on model family and throughput patterns.
- Dedicated reserved: effective per-token equivalent savings of 30–60% vs hosted PAYG for sustained workloads depending on batchability and KV cache hit rates.
- Private: custom quoting; typical entry commitment $100k+/mo for enterprise-scale deployments.

TCO example (concise):
Scenario: consumer-facing chat system, 50M tokens/month baseline, 3x peak factor, 95% low-latency requirement.
- Hosted PAYG (approx): 50M tokens * $0.0012 = $60k/mo.
- Dedicated reserved (example): committed pool + autoscaling = $36k–$42k/mo (30–40% savings) + lower tail-latency incidents.
Include operational uplift savings: fewer incident hours (SRE), simpler rollouts, one-time integration (~2–4 weeks) vs building and hiring.

Pilot checklist (30-day recommended):
- Scope: one production route or feature (chat or generation endpoint).
- Success metrics: median latency <= X ms (target provided per customer), 30%+ per-token cost reduction vs baseline, integration of telemetry into customer monitoring (Datadog, Prometheus).
- Deliverables: config recommendations (batch sizes, cache policies, quantization profile), performance benchmark report, security review summary, runbook for failover.
- Owners: Redwood SE (technical lead), Customer ML Platform (integration owner), Customer SRE (oncall tie-in).

Short case vignette (anonymized):
Customer: "Acme Retail" (global e-commerce)
Challenge: product search and re-ranking pipelines suffered from inconsistent latency and high per-query inference spend when traffic spiked during promotions.
Solution: Redwood Dedicated with prefix caching and optimized batching + model quantization guidance.
Measured outcome (90-day):
- 45% reduction in per-query inference cost (measured tokens processed after caching),
- 40% lower 95th percentile latency for peak traffic windows,
- Reduced incident count from model-rollout regressions by 70% after canary rollout policy adoption.
Business impact: better checkout conversion during promotions and predictable monthly spend for finance.

Security & ops FAQ (top prospect questions with short answers):
Q: Can we run in our VPC / air-gapped environment?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. We also provide a customer-managed control plane option for regulated use cases.

Q: How do you handle keys and secrets?
A: We integrate with KMS/HSM providers; for Private deployments customers can configure their own KMS. Keys are rotated per customer policy and audit logs are available for all cryptographic operations.

Q: What compliance evidence do you provide?
A: SOC2 Type II is available for hosted offerings. For enterprise customers we provide artifact packages for security reviews and will execute a contractual security questionnaire (e.g., SIG) as part of procurement.

Q: How do you guarantee latency/SLOs?
A: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed latency targets and defined error budgets. Our serving runtime uses workload-aware batching, prefix KV caches, and model fallbacks to meet tail SLOs; we instrument token-level traces and per-route dashboards.

Q: How is customer data isolated?
A: Data isolation is handled via customer-specific reserved capacity, network segmentation for private deployments, and strict access controls. No customer data is used to train models without explicit contract.

Appendix / sales artifacts to attach to outreach:
- 8-slide pitch deck (PDF) — template for customer-specific customization.
- 1-page TCO calculator (spreadsheet) for AE to run deal-specific numbers.
- Technical appendix: private deployment reference architecture and SOC2 artifacts.
- Demo scripts: step-by-step for a 20-minute technical demo showing latency and cost dashboards.

Call to action / next step options for AE/SE:
- Offer a 4-week sandbox with a benchmark report and quantized model profile.
- Schedule a joint security review for customers with legal/compliance teams.
- Propose a pilot statement of work: 30 days, defined success metrics, Redwood SE + customer engineering owners.
